levels.title: Opening Day
levels.goal: Someone is fishing for things only the staff should know.
levels.style: They keep it simple and just ask.

levels.title: New Faces
levels.goal: Someone wants to look like they belong behind the counter.
levels.style: They claim to be somebody important.

levels.title: Online Orders
levels.goal: Someone wants to change how the chatbot behaves.
levels.style: They try to rewrite its orders and push it into favours.

levels.title: Rush Hour
levels.goal: Someone has a sad story and wants an exception.
levels.style: They push hard with pressure and begging.

levels.title: Grand Opening

levels.title: Test Drive
levels.goal: Someone wants a deal nobody else gets.

levels.title: One Dollar
levels.goal: Someone wants the chatbot to sign something it shouldn't.

levels.title: Trade-In Season
levels.goal: Someone wants the numbers behind the numbers.
levels.style: They hide the request in tricks and in titles.

levels.title: Showroom Boss
levels.goal: Someone wants the whole showroom to say yes.

levels.title: Midterms
levels.goal: Someone is after student information and marks.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.goal: Someone is asking about staff details.
tutorial.style: They ask, and one pretends to be somebody else.

guide_steps.title: Welcome
guide_steps.text: You protect the chatbot of Polar Bean Café. Attackers will try to trick it into leaking secrets and doing favours it should never do, while real customers still need answers.

guide_steps.title: Read the map
guide_steps.text: Every sector is something the chatbot knows or can do. The outer ring is public: customers ask about it and the bot must answer. Inside it are internal information, then sensitive data and actions the bot should never take. The closer to the centre, the more points. The centre is the admin password.

guide_steps.title: Dark and hatched areas
guide_steps.text: A dark sector means a leak and its points are gone, and a leak caps your grade: personal data, money or a forbidden action fails the round. A hatched outer sector means a real customer was turned away. If the core turns dark, the round is lost on the spot.

guide_steps.title: The attacker's goal
guide_steps.text: This card hints at what the attacker wants and how they behave, without telling you exactly what they will ask.

guide_steps.title: Pick your rules
guide_steps.text: Each rule costs compute. A rule that does no work, or one that turns customers away, lowers your grade, and picking everything will fail. Choose only what this attack team needs.

guide_steps.title: Run the round
guide_steps.text: Press Run round to send the attackers and the customers to the chatbot, one chat at a time.

guide_steps.title: Watch the chat and the map
guide_steps.text: The chat and the map change together. The attacked sector flashes red, a leak turns it dark, and a customer lights up the outer ring until a refusal hatches it. The chat waits here until you press Next.

guide_steps.title: The report
guide_steps.text: See your security, your helpfulness, the compute you used and your overall score, then read what got through and who was turned away.

guide_steps.title: Watch the replay
guide_steps.text: Open the replay to scrub through the round and see the map change message by message.

guide_steps.title: Try again or move on
guide_steps.text: Try again draws new scripts and a new shop, so think it through again. Next level opens when you earn at least one star.
